tagline: Fifteen minutes from Amsterdam, Haarlem has a grand Grote Markt, the Frans Hals Museum, hidden almshouse courtyards and the tulip fields of Keukenhof nearby.
overview: Haarlem is the capital of North Holland and a relaxed alternative to nearby Amsterdam. Its Grote Markt, one of the most beautiful squares in the country, is dominated by the Great Church of St Bavo, whose organ was played by a young Mozart.

The city was a centre of the Dutch Golden Age, and the Frans Hals Museum shows portraits by the master who lived here. The Teylers Museum, opened in 1784, is the oldest museum in the Netherlands, and dozens of hofjes, quiet almshouse courtyards, hide behind doors around the centre.

Haarlem is surrounded by the bulb fields of the Bollenstreek, which bloom in spring, and Keukenhof gardens are a short ride away. The dunes and beach at Zandvoort are about 15 minutes by train, and De Adriaan windmill stands on the Spaarne river.
